title: GATSim: Urban mobility simulation with generative agents
journal: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
authors: Qi Liu; Can Li; Wanjing Ma
abstract: Traditional agent-based urban mobility simulations often rely on rigid rule-based systems that struggle to capture the complexity, adaptability, and behavioral diversity inherent in human travel decision making. Inspired by recent advancements in large language models and AI agent technologies, we introduce GATSim, a novel framework that leverages these advancements to simulate urban mobility using generative agents with dedicated cognitive structures. GATSim agents are characterized by diverse socioeconomic profiles, individual lifestyles, and evolving preferences shaped through psychologically informed memory systems and lifelong learning. The main contributions of this work are: 1) a comprehensive architecture that integrates urban mobility foundation model with agent cognitive systems and transport simulation environment; 2) a hierarchical memory designed for efficient retrieval of contextually relevant information, incorporating spatial and temporal associations; 3) planning and reactive mechanisms for modeling adaptive mobility behaviors which integrate a multi-scale reflection process to transform specific travel experiences into generalized behavioral insights. Experiments indicate that generative agents perform competitively with human annotators in role-playing scenarios, while naturally producing realistic macroscopic traffic patterns. The code for the prototype implementation is publicly available at https://github.com/qiliuchn/gatsim .
abstractZh: 传统基于智能体的城市移动模拟通常依赖刚性的规则系统，难以捕捉人类出行决策内在的复杂性、适应性和行为多样性。受大语言模型与人工智能体技术近期进展启发，本文提出GATSim，一种利用具有专门认知结构的生成式智能体模拟城市移动的新框架。GATSim智能体具有多样社会经济画像、个人生活方式，以及通过具有心理学依据的记忆系统和终身学习不断演化的偏好。本文主要贡献包括：（1）整合城市移动基础模型、智能体认知系统与交通仿真环境的综合架构；（2）结合空间和时间关联、用于高效检索情境相关信息的层级记忆；（3）用于适应性移动行为建模的规划与反应机制，并整合多尺度反思过程，将具体出行经历转化为一般化行为认识。实验表明，生成式智能体在角色扮演场景中的表现可与人类标注者竞争，同时能自然生成真实的宏观交通模式。原型实现代码公开于https://github.com/qiliuchn/gatsim 。
